1.why: Server-side authorization checks enforce that only the authenticated account owner (ACCOUNT_ID) can access MFA endpoints.

2.why: The same verification code does not work for any other user; codes are session-bound and single-use.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated on logout or rotation; enabling MFA does not explicitly invalidate prior sessions, but session rotation occurs on authentication.

4.why: OTP shared secrets and backup codes are stored encrypted (AES-GCM) or hashed (SHA-256 with salt) at rest.

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using cryptographically secure RNG (crypto.getRandomValues).

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are never stored in browser storage or non-HttpOnly cookies; session cookies are HttpOnly.

7.why: Server-side input validation (email, phone, OTP, etc.) is performed with strict allow-lists and sanitization.

8.why: Client-side output is contextually encoded (escapeHTML) to prevent XSS.

9.why: Redirects are not explicitly handled in the code, but the system restricts navigation to internal paths via trustedOrigins and CSP.

10.why: Secure headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) are set in the headers function.

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are never exposed in logs, URLs, or error output; stack traces are suppressed.

13.why: Verification codes (identity codes) are single-use and expire after IDENTITY_CODE_MS (3 minutes).

14.why: Repeated failed verification attempts are rate-limited (MAX_ATTEMPTS=5) and locked out (LOCK_MS=10 minutes).

15.why: Session identifiers are rotated on authentication (rotateSession), have idle (15 min) and absolute (8 hour) timeouts, and are invalidated on logout.
